page: Amazon Web Services c6gn.12xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and powered by custom 64-bit Arm-based AWS Graviton2 processors. The configuration features 48 physical cores executing 48 dedicated vCPUs with a single thread per core at a base frequency of 2.5 GHz, utilizing the ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 microarchitecture. Memory capacity stands at 96.0 GB, providing a strict 1:2 vCPU-to-memory allocation of 2.0 GB per core. The instance includes 64 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 32 MB L3 cache. It contains no onboard GPUs and no bundled local instance storage, relying on external network-attached volumes for persistent data operations.

Network performance is a core differentiator for the c6gn series, delivering 75 Gbps of baseline networking bandwidth. In compute benchmarks, the 48 independent physical cores achieve strong multi-core processing throughput, evidenced by a stress-ng multi-core score of 72814.16 placing it in the top 25 percent. Conversely, single-thread performance benchmarks reflect moderate scores, with single-core Geekbench rating at 974.0 and single-thread gzip compression at 20.35 GB/sec. Memory read bandwidth reaches up to 2839.42 GB/sec for cached 16 KB blocks and 167.25 GB/sec for uncached 256 MB blocks, aligning with the expected profile of high-throughput Arm architecture.

By delivering 48 dedicated physical cores without simultaneous multithreading overhead, the c6gn.12xlarge provides high resource density and sustained parallel execution. Because this server lacks local NVMe disks, overall storage costs depend on attached EBS performance tiers. It is well matched for horizontally scaled network appliances, static web delivery clusters achieving over 40 GB/sec throughput, multi-threaded container workloads, media transcoding, and high-volume Redis caches handling over 58 million SET operations per second.
description: Amazon Web Services c6gn.12xlarge is an Arm-based compute-optimized virtual server running on the AWS Nitro System. Equipped with 48 dedicated physical cores and 48 vCPUs based on the AWS Graviton2 Neoverse-N1 architecture at 2.5 GHz, it supplies 96.0 GB of system memory, matching a 1:2 core-to-memory ratio. The instance features 75 Gbps baseline network bandwidth without local NVMe storage or dedicated GPU hardware. Benchmark results display strong multi-threaded capabilities, including a multi-core stress-ng rating in the top 25 percent, balanced by moderate single-thread execution speeds. The architecture achieves consistent parallel scaling without hyperthreading contention, making it cost-efficient for core-dense applications. Suitable deployments include high-throughput network firewalls, load balancing layers, multi-threaded CI/CD compilation, in-memory caching systems, and distributed web serving.
